title: Great Principality of Duklja
capsule: Duklja (Latin: Dioclea) was a South Slavic principality in the coastal highlands of present-day Montenegro that had become the leading Serb polity after Stefan Vojislav threw off Byzantine overlordship in the 1040s. In this window it was ruled by his son Mihailo I (Mihailo Vojislavljević, r. c. 1046–1081), who balanced ties to Byzantium—marrying into the imperial family and holding the court title of protostrator—against expansion at the empire's expense, conquering neighbouring Rascia in the 1060s. In 1072 Mihailo intervened in the anti-Byzantine uprising in Macedonia, dispatching his son Constantine Bodin, who was briefly proclaimed 'tsar' by the rebels. The papal recognition of Mihailo as king and Bodin's later expansion over Rascia and Bosnia came only after this period.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core coastal territory of Duklja is identified through Byzantine and papal sources, but the extent of its inland dominion over Rascia and Bosnia is only approximately attested and varied considerably over time.
